sets: Part B · Conceptual MCQs
Which termini can a standard DNA ligase join at a clean nick?
A. 3′-P and 5′-OH|B. 3′-OH and 5′-P|C. 3′-P and 5′-P|D. 3′-OH and 5′-OH
B
The 3′ hydroxyl attacks the activated 5′ phosphate. A lacks both necessary groups; C lacks a free 3′ hydroxyl and D lacks the activated phosphate.
What distinguishes a nick from a gap?
A. A nick lacks a backbone bond but no nucleotide|B. A nick interrupts both strands|C. A gap always contains a modified base|D. A nick always carries a mutation
A
A gap lacks nucleotide positions; a nick need not. Neither structure necessarily changes the inherited sequence, and a nick affects one strand.
Which protein coordinates mammalian SSBR through interactions with multiple enzymes?
A. RAD51|B. XRCC1|C. FtsZ|D. LexA
B
XRCC1 is a scaffold in SSBR; RAD51 promotes homologous pairing, FtsZ participates in division and LexA regulates bacterial SOS genes.
Which activity directly removes a blocking 3′ phosphate and can phosphorylate a 5′ hydroxyl?
A. PNKP|B. Pol β|C. Ku70|D. RAD51
A
PNKP corrects terminal chemistry. Pol β performs synthesis, Ku recognizes duplex ends, and RAD51 promotes homologous interactions.
PARP1 consumes which substrate to generate poly(ADP-ribose)?
A. dATP|B. NAD⁺|C. UDP-glucose|D. GTP
B
NAD⁺ supplies ADP-ribose units. PARP signaling does not directly synthesize DNA or seal a nick.
Which mammalian protein complex directly supplies the ligase activity in classical NHEJ?
A. MRN|B. Ku–DNA-PKcs|C. XRCC4–LIG4|D. RPA–RAD51
C
Ligase IV catalyzes joining and XRCC4 supports it. MRN processes or organizes breaks; Ku–DNA-PKcs participates in recognition and regulation.
What does DNA-PKcs principally catalyze?
A. DNA ligation|B. Protein phosphorylation|C. DNA base excision|D. RNA transcription
B
DNA-PKcs is a protein kinase using ATP; DNA ligase IV completes phosphodiester joining.
When can NHEJ produce exact restoration?
A. Never|B. Only when RAD51 is absent|C. When the original compatible ends are rejoined without sequence alteration|D. Only after deleting both ends
C
End joining does not intrinsically require nucleotide loss. Compatible ends can be precisely sealed; neither RAD51 absence nor trimming is a prerequisite.
What is the product of standard 5′-strand end resection?
A. 5′ single-stranded tails|B. 3′ single-stranded tails|C. Two RNA primers|D. A covalently closed chromosome
B
Preferential loss of the 5′-terminated strands leaves 3′ tails that can prime synthesis after pairing with a homologous donor.
What is the key role of BRCA2 in conventional HR?
A. Load RAD51 onto ssDNA|B. Cut all DNA ends|C. Ligate DNA by ATP|D. Synthesize ubiquitin
A
BRCA2 helps assemble RAD51 on resected ssDNA. It is not the final ligase, a universal nuclease or a ubiquitin-synthesizing enzyme.
Why is HR favored in S/G2 relative to G1 in typical mammalian cells?
A. Ligase IV exists only in G1|B. Sister chromatids and resection-promoting regulation become available|C. DNA synthesis is chemically impossible in G1|D. Homologous chromosomes disappear in G1
B
A sister donor is available following local replication, and cell-cycle regulation favors resection. NHEJ remains active in S/G2; homologs do not disappear in G1.
What is the immediate objective of TLS?
A. Excise the damaged parental base|B. Seal every DSB|C. Continue DNA synthesis using a lesion-containing template|D. Degrade the whole chromosome
C
TLS directly bypasses a lesion during synthesis. Excision and DSB repair solve different substrate problems.
Which example contradicts the claim that all TLS is necessarily mutagenic?
A. Pol η inserting adenines opposite a thymine CPD|B. Ku protecting ends|C. LexA binding an operator|D. PNKP correcting a 3′ phosphate
A
Pol η is adapted to bypass certain CPDs accurately. The remaining options describe other reactions and do not test TLS fidelity.
Which signal commonly promotes recruitment of eukaryotic TLS polymerases?
A. PCNA monoubiquitination|B. DNA ligase IV removal|C. FtsZ polymerization|D. LexA accumulation
A
PCNA modification supports damage-associated polymerase exchange. FtsZ and LexA belong to bacterial systems.
Which bacterial protein is the SOS repressor in E. coli?
A. RecA|B. LexA|C. SulA|D. UmuC
B
LexA binds SOS operators. RecA stimulates LexA self-cleavage, SulA affects division and UmuC contributes to Pol V.
Which statement correctly describes SOS induction?
A. LexA stimulates RecA proteolysis|B. Activated RecA promotes LexA self-cleavage|C. FtsZ directly cleaves LexA|D. Pol V transcribes SOS genes
B
The DNA-associated RecA state stimulates LexA's own cleavage reaction, releasing repression; RecA is not an indiscriminate protease.
What is the direct cellular target of SulA in E. coli division control?
A. FtsZ assembly|B. RAD51 loading|C. DNA ligase IV|D. Telomerase
A
SulA inhibits FtsZ-dependent division. Its role buys time for recovery rather than directly repairing DNA.
Which E. coli complex initiates repair of many duplex DNA ends?
A. RecBCD|B. ORC|C. DNA-PKcs|D. RNA polymerase II
A
RecBCD processes broken duplex ends and supports RecA loading; ORC and RNA polymerase II are eukaryotic systems.
Which outcome is characteristic of single-strand annealing between direct repeats?
A. Always exact restoration|B. Deletion of the intervening region and one repeat|C. Conversion of DNA into RNA|D. Removal of a CPD by light
B
Annealing of exposed repeat sequences eliminates the intervening DNA and redundant repeat. This is not conventional sister-directed restoration.
What is the primary difference between classical NHEJ and template-guided HR?
A. Only HR makes a phosphodiester bond|B. NHEJ uses no extended homologous donor, HR normally does|C. NHEJ is bacterial only|D. HR requires no DNA synthesis in any context
B
Both can restore covalent DNA continuity. Their defining difference is the use of donor information, not species or an absolute difference in ligation.
Part C · Analytical and experimental MCQs
A repaired DNA patch incorporates labeled dNTPs but persists as a nick. Which activity is most directly implicated?
A. Gap filling|B. Final ligation|C. Base pairing|D. DNA unwinding
B
Incorporation establishes that synthesis occurred; it does not establish phosphodiester continuity at the final junction. A ligation defect is most consistent with the combination.
A clean nick and a 3′-P/5′-OH nick are exposed to ligase alone. Only the former is sealed. Adding PNKP rescues the latter. What follows?
A. PNKP substitutes for ligase|B. PNKP restores ligatable chemistry|C. DNA ligase requires a DSB|D. PNKP removes entire damaged genes
B
The selective rescue shows the importance of terminal processing. Ligation still supplies the final bond; the experiment does not show that PNKP ligates.
Two genetically identical mammalian populations are in G1 or G2. A donor-marker HR reporter is induced equally. G2 shows higher reporter restoration. Best explanation?
A. Only G2 contains ATP|B. G2 favors template-directed repair and resection|C. G1 cannot repair any DSB|D. G2 cannot perform NHEJ
B
G2 offers sister DNA and appropriate regulation. The experiment supports a cell-cycle association, not the absolute exclusion of other pathways.
A mutant shows fewer colonies after irradiation and is restored by the normal gene. What is justified without other assays?
A. The gene is necessarily a ligase|B. It contributes to survival under the tested conditions|C. Every surviving mutant has an altered sequence|D. The gene is necessarily involved in TLS
B
Rescue supports a causal contribution to survival. Specific chemistry requires independent substrate or enzyme evidence.
A broken reporter lacks two bases. The donor contains a nearby silent marker. Restored reporters acquire the marker. Most direct inference?
A. End trimming alone occurred|B. Donor sequence information was transferred|C. All breaks are repaired by NHEJ|D. Marker acquisition proves a crossover
B
The marker distinguishes donor-dependent copying from direct joining of original ends. It does not establish whether a crossover occurred.
A G1-enriched mutant has reduced HR reporter activity. Its purified RAD51 behaves normally. Best next control?
A. Remove all DNA|B. Compare phase-matched cells and reporter delivery|C. Count only total culture mass|D. Assume RAD51 is inactive
B
Cell-cycle composition and assay eligibility can explain the difference. Normal purified activity does not settle recruitment or regulation.
At a break between two 12-base direct repeats, sequencing shows loss of the intervening interval and one repeat. Which conclusion is strongest?
A. Consistent with repeat-mediated annealing|B. Unambiguously proves POLQ dependence|C. Proves no DNA processing|D. Establishes exact restoration
A
The product fits an annealing mechanism. Genetic tests are needed to distinguish routes with overlapping junction patterns.
Ku-deficient cells retain some repaired junctions. Which interpretation is valid?
A. Ku is irrelevant|B. All junctions are precise|C. Other pathways may restore some continuity|D. The cells lack DNA damage
C
Repair is partly redundant; residual joining can be due to alternative mechanisms. Neither product accuracy nor absence of damage follows.
A replication fork encounters a nick and creates a one-ended DSB. Which outcome is least suitable as a general solution?
A. Access an intact homologous template|B. Restore a productive replication structure|C. Join the end to an unrelated chromosome end|D. Temporarily delay progression
C
The unmatched end cannot be safely paired arbitrarily. Incorrect joining risks rearrangement rather than restoration of the original fork.
A POLH mutant and wild type remove UV photoproducts at the same rate; mutant nascent DNA remains shorter. Which process is primarily implicated?
A. Lesion-specific bypass|B. Photoproduct formation|C. Base excision of every lesion|D. Chromosome centromere loss
A
Normal removal with defective synthesis recovery supports a tolerance defect; cell-cycle and baseline replication controls strengthen the inference.
Polymerase X copies undamaged DNA accurately but stops at a dimer. Y bypasses the dimer with correct incorporation but is inaccurate on normal DNA. Best biological strategy?
A. Permanently replace X with Y|B. Restrict Y to appropriate damaged substrates|C. Prevent all nucleotide incorporation|D. Remove every sliding clamp
B
Transient polymerase switching combines normal replication fidelity with lesion-specific capacity, avoiding unnecessary mutagenesis.
A PCNA Lys164 modification-site mutant has normal purified Pol η activity but poor UV-associated synthesis. What is a plausible mechanism?
A. Impaired polymerase access or regulation|B. Pol η has changed catalytic sequence necessarily|C. DNA synthesis runs 3′ to 5′|D. All UV lesions are absent
A
The clamp modification influences cellular pathway selection. Purified enzyme activity can remain intact while recruitment is impaired.
A noncleavable LexA retains operator binding; damaged cells show normal RecA accumulation but low SOS reporter transcription. Why?
A. LexA repression cannot be relieved normally|B. FtsZ directly transcribes the reporter|C. DNA has no single-stranded regions|D. LexA is the bypass polymerase
A
The regulatory block lies at repressor cleavage. Normal RecA abundance is not sufficient to overcome noncleavable LexA.
A strain has constitutive SOS reporter expression in the absence of detectable breaks. Which statement is justified?
A. All DNA must be broken|B. The regulatory state can be altered independently of lesion burden|C. Pol V is necessarily maximally active|D. The cells lack LexA target genes
B
Reporter activity measures promoter regulation. Additional activation requirements and the absence of detectable lesions preclude the other conclusions.
A SulA-deficient strain induces SOS genes normally but divides sooner after damage. What is the most direct missing function?
A. Division delay|B. LexA cleavage|C. DNA ligation|D. Removal of thymine dimers
A
SulA inhibits division via FtsZ. Other SOS functions may remain induced in this mutant.
A mutant gives more persistent γH2AX foci but normal levels of correct reporter junctions. What should be tested before inferring a generalized repair defect?
A. Marker persistence and other damage classes|B. Whether all foci are mutations|C. Whether H2AX is a ligase|D. Nothing; foci prove exact break counts
A
Signaling foci are indirect measures and the reporter samples a particular substrate. Additional physical and functional assays are needed.
In hypothetical populations A and B, damage-marker foci disappear faster in A, but A has more deletions in repaired junctions. Which conclusion is valid?
A. A necessarily preserves sequence better|B. Speed of signal loss and sequence fidelity are different endpoints|C. B has no repair|D. Both pathways are proven identical
B
Rapid disappearance of a signal can accompany mutagenic joining. Sequencing gives complementary information about accuracy.
A donor-dependent repair reporter decreases after deletion of a regulator, but an unrelated reporter delivery control also decreases. What is the best interpretation?
A. HR is conclusively blocked|B. Delivery differences confound pathway inference|C. All cells are in G2|D. The regulator is a DNA nuclease
B
Fewer eligible cells can reduce raw reporter output. Normalize to successful delivery and viable cells before assigning a repair defect.
A mutant can bind a break but an inactive version of its protein fails to restore repair. A functional version restores repair. What is supported?
A. Binding alone is insufficient under these conditions|B. The protein never binds DNA|C. Catalysis is irrelevant|D. Every repair gene acts identically
A
The comparison suggests an additional activity beyond binding is needed. It does not establish the exact catalytic step without further evidence.
A homologous donor carries allele a at a damaged A locus. The repaired recipient and original donor both carry a. Which genetic outcome is consistent?
A. Local loss of heterozygosity|B. Obligatory chromosome loss|C. No sequence change possible|D. RNA editing
A
Copying donor information can change the recipient allele without losing a chromosome. HR is not necessarily restoration of the original allele.
Numerical and multiple-statement reasoning
A treated population yields 360 colonies and a matched untreated population yields 1,800. What is survival?
B
360/1,800 = 0.20, or 20%. The ratio assumes comparable input and plating conditions.
From 10,000 initial viable cells, 2,000 survive and 30 survivors are mutant. What is the mutant fraction among survivors?
B
30/2,000 = 0.015 = 1.5%. 30/10,000 = 0.3% is relative to initial input, not survivors.
A population has 25% survival and a mutant fraction of 0.04 among survivors. What fraction of initial cells are mutant survivors?
A
Multiply S × f = 0.25 × 0.04 = 0.01. The result is 1% of the original input.
In a hypothetical first-order model, 100 breaks fall to 25 in 4 h. What is the half-time?
A. 1 h|B. 2 h|C. 4 h|D. 8 h
B
A fourfold reduction represents two half-times, so t½ = 4/2 = 2 h. This assumes no new breaks and first-order disappearance.
Using a first-order model with k = 0.3466 h⁻¹, what fraction remains after 4 h?
B
exp(−0.3466 × 4) ≈ exp(−1.3864) ≈ 0.25. k has inverse-time units.
Reporter A gives 300 positives among 1,500 eligible cells; reporter B gives 180 among 600. Which has higher positive fraction?
A. A|B. B|C. Equal|D. Cannot calculate
B
A = 20%, B = 30%. Raw positives alone would reverse the apparent comparison. The percentages apply only to the reporter-defined endpoints.
Select correct statements: I. NHEJ can be precise. II. HR can copy a donor variant. III. TLS always removes lesions. IV. γH2AX is a signaling marker.
A. I, II, IV|B. II, III|C. I, III|D. III, IV
A
I, II and IV are correct. TLS completes synthesis without necessarily removing the template lesion.
Select correct statements: I. RecA promotes LexA self-cleavage. II. SulA directly ligates DNA. III. Pol II has proofreading activity. IV. E. coli universally uses Ku–LigD.
A. I and III|B. I and IV|C. II and III|D. All
A
SulA regulates division, not ligation. Ku–LigD is found in certain bacteria but is not the standard E. coli repair system.
Match 1. Ku; 2. RPA; 3. LIG4; 4. Pol η to P. ssDNA binding; Q. DSB end recognition; R. joining; S. CPD bypass.
A
Ku binds duplex ends; RPA coats ssDNA; ligase IV catalyzes NHEJ sealing; Pol η bypasses suitable UV photoproducts.
Match 1. G1; 2. S/G2; 3. 3′-P nick; 4. LexA noncleavable to P. restricted SOS induction; Q. sister-donor availability; R. favors NHEJ for two-ended breaks; S. end processing required.
A
The matching follows template availability, terminal chemistry and repression logic, not an absolute restriction of NHEJ to G1.
Assertion–Reason
Assertion: Classical NHEJ can restore an original DNA sequence. Reason: Compatible ends may be sealed without nucleotide removal or addition.
A. Both true, reason explains assertion|B. Both true, reason does not explain|C. Assertion true, reason false|D. Assertion false, reason true
A
The reason establishes how direct rejoining can preserve every nucleotide. Mutagenicity depends on processing and alignment.
Assertion: TLS can improve completion of DNA synthesis without eliminating the original lesion. Reason: A specialized polymerase can use a lesion-containing template directly.
A. Both true, reason explains assertion|B. Both true, reason does not explain|C. Assertion true, reason false|D. Assertion false, reason true
A
The bypass polymerase solves the copying problem without chemically reversing or excising the original lesion.
Assertion: HR predominates exclusively in all S/G2 mammalian cells. Reason: Sister chromatids are available after replication.
A. Both true, reason explains assertion|B. Both true, reason does not explain|C. Assertion true, reason false|D. Assertion false, reason true
D
Sister availability favors HR but does not exclude NHEJ or guarantee predominance for every substrate.
Assertion: RecA deficiency can affect both recombinational recovery and SOS induction. Reason: RecA participates in homologous interactions and stimulates LexA self-cleavage.
A. Both true, reason explains assertion|B. Both true, reason does not explain|C. Assertion true, reason false|D. Assertion false, reason true
A
Two mechanistically distinct RecA functions can explain the combined phenotype.
Assertion: A decrease in the proportion of mutant survivors necessarily means improved DNA repair. Reason: Mutation fraction among survivors is conditioned on survival.
A. Both true, reason explains assertion|B. Both true, reason does not explain|C. Assertion true, reason false|D. Assertion false, reason true
D
Selection of survivors can change the measured fraction. Survival and mutation frequency must be measured separately.

definitions: One missing backbone linkage without a missing nucleotide.
One or more missing nucleotides in a strand.
Discontinuity in both strands of a duplex.
Processing that exposes ssDNA, commonly 3′ tails for HR.
End joining without an extended homologous donor.
Direct DNA synthesis across a lesion-containing template.
Bypass using alternative undamaged sister-derived information.
Detected mutant survivors divided by eligible survivors.
traps: Ligation cannot fill a missing nucleotide.
A 3′ phosphate is not a primer hydroxyl.
PARP1 and XRCC1 are not DNA ligases.
HR need not restore the original allele.
Microhomology is not unique evidence for an alternative pathway.
TLS does not necessarily remove damage.
Pol η can accurately bypass suitable CPDs.
LexA cleaves itself with stimulation by RecA.
Fewer γH2AX foci do not prove exact repair.
Survival and mutant frequency have different denominators.

Predict effects of end-processing, ligation and HR defects.
